questions.question: In field hockey, ________ occurs when a player pushes the ball and raises it off the ground.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**flick**__

__
 
• A **flick** occurs when a player pushes the ball and raises it off the ground in field hockey.
 
• This technique is often used to lift the ball over an opponent's stick or to make an aerial pass.
 
• It requires precise control and timing to execute effectively.
 
• Flicks are also used in penalty corners to shoot at the goal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **bully** is a method used to restart play, similar to a face-off in ice hockey.
 
• A **slap** involves hitting the ball with a slapping motion, keeping it close to the ground.
 
• A **centre pass** is used to start or restart the game from the center of the field.
 
• Field hockey is a game played between two teams of eleven players, using sticks to hit a ball into the opponent's goal.

questions.question: The method of separating a mixture of soluble solids by dissolving them in a suitable hot solvent and then lowering the temperature slowly is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fractional crystallisation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fractional crystallisation** is a method of separating a mixture of soluble solids.
 
• This process involves dissolving the mixture in a suitable hot solvent.
 
• The temperature is then slowly lowered, which causes the different components to crystallise at different temperatures.
 
• This method is used to purify substances and separate components based on their solubility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sublimation** is a process where a solid changes directly into a gas without going through a liquid phase.
 
• **Azeotropic distillation** is used to separate components of a mixture by distillation, involving an azeotrope.
 
• **Dephlegmation** is a process used in the distillation of mixtures to separate components with close boiling points.

questions.question: How is the structure of health infrastructure and health care system in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three-tier system**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The health infrastructure and health care system in India is organized in a **three-tier system**.
 
• This system comprises the **primary, secondary, and tertiary** levels of care.
 
• **Primary level** includes sub-centers and primary health centers (PHCs) which are the first point of contact for the community.
 
• **Secondary level** includes community health centers (CHCs) and district hospitals that provide more specialized care.
 
• **Tertiary level** includes medical colleges and specialized hospitals which offer advanced medical services and treatments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India's health care system is governed by both the central and state governments, with public and private sectors playing significant roles.
 
• The central government is responsible for formulating national health policies and providing technical and financial support to the states.
 
• State governments are primarily responsible for the delivery of health services and implementation of health programs.
 
• The National Health Mission (NHM) aims to strengthen the health system, particularly in rural and underserved areas.
 
• India's health care system faces challenges such as resource constraints, unequal access to services, and the need for improved infrastructure and workforce.

questions.question: Which group of animals has a segmented spinal column together with a few primitive forms in which the backbone is represented by a notochord?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vertebrata**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vertebrata** is the group of animals that have a segmented spinal column.
 
• This group includes not only advanced organisms with a developed backbone but also some primitive forms in which the backbone is represented by a notochord.
 
• The notochord is a flexible rod-like structure that forms the main support of the body in these primitive organisms.
 
• Examples of vertebrates include mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fish.
 
• The presence of a segmented spinal column is a key characteristic that differentiates vertebrates from other animal groups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vertebrates** are part of the phylum Chordata, which is characterized by the presence of a notochord at some stage of development.
 
• The notochord is replaced by the vertebral column in most adult vertebrates, providing more structural support and protection for the spinal cord.
 
• Other distinguishing features of vertebrates include a well-developed brain, a closed circulatory system, and an endoskeleton made of bone or cartilage.
 
• The evolutionary development of the vertebral column has allowed vertebrates to become highly adaptable and occupy a wide range of ecological niches.
 
• Vertebrates are the most complex and diverse group of animals, with over 66,000 species described to date.

questions.question: How might ICT enhance the openness of e-land records?

options.text: Enabling quick search and retrieval of land records
Reducing the need for land surveys and assessments
Facilitating manual record updates and amendments
Enforcing strict regulations on land transactions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Enabling quick search and retrieval of land records**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Enabling quick search and retrieval of land records** is one of the primary ways ICT can enhance the openness of e-land records.
 
• ICT facilitates the digitization and online availability of land records, making it easier for stakeholders to access information efficiently.
 
• With digital records, transparency is increased as the data is less prone to tampering and unauthorized alterations.
 
• ICT systems can provide real-time updates and tracking of land records, reducing delays and increasing the reliability of information.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ICT stands for **Information and Communication Technology**, which encompasses various digital tools and systems used to manage, process, and share information.
 
• Implementation of ICT in land records management can significantly reduce administrative costs and human errors.
 
• By improving access to land records, ICT can help in resolving disputes and enhancing land tenure security.
 
• ICT-driven platforms often include features like GIS mapping, which provides visual representation and spatial analysis of land data.
 
• Electronic land records can also facilitate better planning and development by providing accurate and up-to-date information to policymakers.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT associated with the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956?

options.text: A system of licenses for the private sector was introduced.
It classified industries into three categories.
It formed the basis of the Third Five Year Plan.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It formed the basis of the Third Five Year Plan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 did not form the basis of the Third Five Year Plan. The Third Five Year Plan was introduced in 1961 and had different objectives and goals.
 
• The resolution did introduce a system of licenses for the private sector, classifying industries into three categories, and promoted regional equality.
 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 aimed at the establishment of a socialistic pattern of society where the state would play a dominant role in the industrial sector.
 
• It laid the foundation for the development of public sector enterprises and sought to reduce regional imbalances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 was a significant policy document that shaped the industrial landscape of post-independence India.
 
• It categorized industries into three schedules: Schedule A included industries exclusively under state control, Schedule B included industries where the state would play a dominant role, and Schedule C included all remaining industries.
 
• The policy aimed to accelerate the rate of growth and industrialization, create more employment opportunities, and reduce income and wealth inequalities.
 
• The policy also aimed at fostering the development of small-scale industries to promote balanced regional growth.

questions.question: Who is known as the ‘Father of Carnatic Music’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Purandara Dasa**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Purandara Dasa** is widely regarded as the 'Father of Carnatic Music'.
 
• He was a renowned composer, vocalist, and a key figure in the development and structuring of Carnatic music, which is a classical music form of Southern India.
 
• Purandara Dasa formulated the basic lessons for teaching Carnatic music, which are still followed today.
 
• He composed thousands of devotional songs, known as 'Devaranamas', in praise of Lord Vishnu.
 
• His contributions laid the foundation for the Carnatic music system, making it easier to learn and practice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Purandara Dasa is believed to have lived between 1484 and 1564.
 
• He is often referred to as the Karnataka Sangeetha Pitamaha (Grandfather of Carnatic Music).
 
• His compositions are mostly in Kannada language, and they cover various aspects of devotion, ethics, and philosophy.
 
• He is credited with structuring music lessons in a graded system which includes Sarale Varase, Janti Varase, Alankara, Lakshana Geethe, and so on.
 
• Purandara Dasa's work has had a lasting impact on the Carnatic music tradition, influencing countless musicians and composers who followed him.

questions.question: Which folk music is based on the Mahabharata with Bhima portrayed as hero?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Pandavani** is a folk music tradition of the Indian state of Chhattisgarh.
 
• This form of music narrates the tales of the Mahabharata, focusing primarily on the heroics of Bhima.
 
• The performance usually involves a lead singer who is accompanied by musicians playing traditional instruments like the tambura and harmonium.
 
• Pandavani is known for its dramatic storytelling style, where the performer often enacts the scenes while singing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mando** is a form of Goan music that blends Indian and Western traditions.
 
• **Dandiya** is a traditional folk dance of Gujarat, often performed during the Navratri festival.
 
• **Alha** is a ballad tradition from the Bundelkhand region of India, narrating the heroic deeds of Alha and Udal.
 
• Pandavani performances are an essential part of the cultural heritage of Chhattisgarh and are cherished for their rich narrative and musical tradition.

questions.question: In his ‘Drain of Wealth’ argument, who among the following stated that Britain was completely draining India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was an Indian political leader, educator, and an early Indian nationalist who is credited with the 'Drain of Wealth' theory.
 
• In his book, **'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'**, Naoroji argued that a significant portion of India's wealth was being drained to Britain, causing widespread poverty in India.
 
• His theory highlighted the economic exploitation of India under British rule and became a key point of criticism against colonial policies.
 
• Naoroji's efforts were instrumental in raising awareness about the economic impact of British colonialism on India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was also known as the 'Grand Old Man of India' and was one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He was the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament, where he advocated for Indian self-rule and economic reforms.
 
• His work laid the foundation for subsequent economic theories and nationalist movements in India.
 
• Naoroji's contributions were crucial in shaping the early phase of the Indian independence struggle.

questions.question: In MS Word, which option allows you to align text in a way that it appears vertically at the bottom of a cell or text box?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Bottom Alignment** allows you to align text in a way that it appears vertically at the bottom of a cell or text box in MS Word.
 
• This option is particularly useful when you want the text to start from the bottom edge of the cell or text box, leaving space above it.
 
• To apply this alignment, select the cell or text box, then go to the "Layout" or "Table Tools Layout" tab, and choose the "Bottom Align" option from the "Alignment" group.
 
• Bottom Alignment is one of several vertical alignment options available in MS Word, which also includes Top Alignment and Center Alignment.

• These alignment options can be accessed from the "Home" tab in the "Paragraph" group or through the "Table Tools Layout" tab when working within a table.
 
• Using these alignment tools effectively can enhance the readability and presentation of your document.
 
• Remember that proper alignment is a key aspect of formatting that contributes to the overall aesthetic and clarity of your document.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India CANNOT be amended with simple majority?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**21**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 21** of the Constitution of India cannot be amended with a simple majority.
 
• Article 21 guarantees the protection of life and personal liberty, stating that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to the procedure established by law.
 
• This article is a fundamental right under Part III of the Constitution and requires a more rigorous process for amendment as outlined in Article 368.
 
• Simple majority amendments are generally for non-fundamental aspects of the Constitution, whereas fundamental rights require a special majority and, in some cases, ratification by at least half of the state legislatures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Articles 2 and 3** relate to the admission or establishment of new states and the formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states, respectively. These can be amended with a simple majority.
 
• **Article 169** provides for the abolition or creation of Legislative Councils in states and can also be amended with a simple majority.
 
• The **Constitution** of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• The Constitution lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.

questions.question: Which amongst the following terms was used for the land given to Brahmins during the Chola empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmadeya**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brahmadeya** was the term used for the land grants given to Brahmins during the Chola empire.
 
• These grants were usually tax-free and were provided to Brahmins to encourage settlement and agricultural development.
 
• The land grants were an important aspect of the Chola administrative and social system, reflecting the high status and respect accorded to Brahmins in society.
 
• Brahmadeya lands were often associated with temples and played a crucial role in the spread of education and culture.
 
• Other terms related to land classification in the Chola period include Shalabhoga (land for maintenance of schools), Tirunmatukkani (land gifted to temples), and Vellanvagai (land of non-Brahmin peasants).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Chola dynasty was one of the longest-ruling dynasties in South Indian history, known for its contributions to art, architecture, and administration.
 
• The Chola rulers implemented an efficient administrative system with a well-organized bureaucracy and local self-government in villages.
 
• The Chola period is also noted for its remarkable achievements in temple architecture, with the Brihadeeswarar Temple being a prime example.
 
• The Chola navy was a dominant maritime force, facilitating trade and cultural exchanges with Southeast Asia.

questions.question: Writ of Mandamus is a Fundamental Right classifiable under:

options.text: the right to freedom of religion

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**constitutional remedies**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Writ of Mandamus** is a judicial remedy in the form of an order from a court to any government, subordinate court, corporation, or public authority to do some specific act which that body is obliged under law to do.
 
• It is classified under **constitutional remedies**, which is a fundamental right provided under **Article 32** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 32 provides the right to individuals to move to the Supreme Court for enforcement of their fundamental rights.
 
• The **Writ of Mandamus** can be issued to enforce the performance of public duties by public authorities and to ensure that they fulfill their legal obligations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Constitution of India** provides for five types of writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo-Warranto, and Certiorari.
 
• These writs are a crucial part of the **judicial review mechanism** in India, ensuring the protection of citizens' rights against any arbitrary actions of the state.
 
• The **right to constitutional remedies** is considered the heart and soul of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, as it is the protector and guarantor of all other fundamental rights.
 
• Article 32 is also known as the "Right to Constitutional Remedies" and is a fundamental right that cannot be suspended, except in cases of emergency as declared by the President of India.
